title: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for oauth-openid-connect trace events.

protocol.description: Plain OAuth 2.0 (delegated authorization) or OpenID Connect (identity on top).

clientType.description: Whether the client has a server to keep a client_secret on.

pkce.description: Whether the code is bound to its requester with a code_verifier / code_challenge pair.

stateCheck.description: Whether the client sends and verifies a `state` parameter.

clock.description: Model time in minutes since the run started.

accessLifetime.description: How long an issued access token stays valid, in minutes.

parties.description: The parties of the protocol and what each of them is holding right now.

id.description: Party id, used by highlight tokens as party:<id>.

role.description: The role this party plays in the protocol.

label.description: Human-readable name: a user, a client_id or a host.

holdings.description: What this party currently knows or holds.

kind.description: What sort of artifact it is; secrets must never reach the front channel.

message.description: The message the current step sends, and the channel it travels on.

from.description: Party id the message leaves; empty when nothing is being sent.

to.description: Party id the message arrives at; empty when nothing is being sent.

channel.description: front = a browser redirect anyone can read; back = direct server-to-server; none = local work.

label.description: The request line or the action, e.g. 'POST https://accounts.provider.com/token'.

params.description: The parameters carried by this message.

steps.description: The stages of the authorization code flow, in order, with how far this run has got.

status.description: pending = not reached; skipped = this grant does not have it; breach = it let through what it should have stopped.

detail.description: Bare token behind the verdict: a scope list, a code, a token id or a reason.

scopes.description: The scopes this flow asked for, and whether the user granted each.

identity.description: Who the client believes the user is; null while it has no basis for an opinion.

source.description: What the client read the identity from; access_token is always the mistake.

verified.description: Whether signature, issuer, audience, expiry and nonce were actually checked.

status.description: HTTP status of this step; null while it is local or still running.

decision.description: risky = it worked and you should not build it; breach = it worked and should not have.

reason.description: Technical code for the refusal, the risk or the breach; null when nothing went wrong.

detail.description: The offending code, token, scope or user; empty when not applicable.

stats.description: Running totals across the whole run.

apiServed.description: API calls the resource server answered.

apiRefused.description: API calls refused for a missing, expired or under-scoped token.

warnings.description: Moves that worked and should not be built that way.

breaches.description: Things that worked and should not have.
